newsitem.title: UK: LVMH's Arnault shakes hands, back to Paris.
newsitem.headline: LVMH's Arnault shakes hands, back to Paris.

text.p: Bernard Arnault, chairman of French luxury goods company LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton, has returned to Paris after visiting three to four shareholders in Guinness and Grand Metropolitan in London on Thursday.
"He is not asking for votes. But he is seeking to explain why he believes his three-way merger delivers better value for shareholders," said a spokesman for Arnault's camp.
Arnault has opposed Guinness and Grand Met's plans for a 24 billion stg merger since it was announced in May, because it threatens to sideline LVMH's drinks division Moet Hennessy.
Arnault's visits on Thursday formed part of informal presentations to institutions that would continue through the summer, said the spokesman.
He plans to return to London next week to see a further three or four institutions, including Schroders.

The spokesman would not say who the institutional shareholders were that Arnault met on Thursday, but described them as having "a long relationship with Bull (George Bull, chairman of Grand Met) and Greener (Tony Greener, chairman of Guinness)."
Arnault needs the support of 25 percent of Grand Met's shareholders to block the merger outright.
He has built up a stake of 11.05 percent in Grand Met and has enough shares in both companies to convene an extraordinary meeting.

LVMH bought nearly 100 million shares in Grand Met on Tuesday to boost its stake from a previous 6.4 percent, while investment fund Mercury Asset Management cut its stake in Grand Met to 0.47 percent from 2.6 percent. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
